note: Three entries were revisited after router runs. Every change is recorded here with its reasoning rather than made quietly, because reclassifying failures after seeing results is what the Phase 6 gate exists to prevent. The test applied in each case: does the correction improve the system, or only the number? R05 and BOTH06 were genuine label errors — correcting them changes no code. N03 stays counted as a miss because fixing it required a real change to the router, which was then made.
variance_note: Three runs of the same prompt produced 21/24, 21/24 and 22/24. BOTH04 and BOTH05 flip between runs; BOTH06 failed consistently, which is what distinguished a genuine label error from noise. At 24 questions each item is 4.2 points, so a single run's headline number is not a measurement. Report the range, not the best run.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: What was SUP-003's defect PPM in August 2026?
questions.why: A single figure from one supplier and one month. Nothing about it needs explaining.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: Which supplier had the worst defect rate over the last 12 months?
questions.why: A ranking. 8D reports exist for several of these suppliers, but extra context is not incompleteness.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: How many defect events were recorded against SUP-009 parts in 2026?
questions.why: A count with a filter. The metric is stated, so no ambiguity.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: Which parts recorded no defects at all in August 2026?
questions.why: Absence, answerable because low-runner parts exist. The five that return are the low runners.

questions.label: NEITHER
questions.question: For each commodity, which part had the worst PPM in the last 12 months?
questions.why: Originally labelled SQL. Corrected to NEITHER after the baseline run: no catalogue query groups by commodity — part_ppm_ranking ranks parts globally. The router read the manifest accurately and the original label assumed a capability that does not exist. This is a catalogue gap, not a routing error.
questions.relabelled: 2026-09-07, after the baseline run. The reason is structural: the capability is absent, so NEITHER is the correct read of what is available. Correcting it does not change the router, which is the test for whether a relabel is legitimate.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: Which defect code accounts for the largest share of SUP-003's defect units?
questions.why: A share-of-total. D-WLD-01 at roughly half, computable without any document.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: What was the root cause of the roof rail splitting?
questions.why: A cause, recorded in 8D-2025-007 D4. SQL can show the spike but cannot say why.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: What corrective action was taken on the missing fasteners issue?
questions.why: An action taken. Lives only in D5 and D6 of 8D-2025-018.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: Which quality issues are still open?
questions.why: Status recorded in the reports. Known flaw: reports_8d.status is a Postgres column, so SQL could in principle answer this — but no catalogue query exposes it. Labelled DOCS because of what was built in Phase 4, not because of a principle. Flagged before the baseline run, not after.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: Has weld porosity at SUP-003 happened before, and what was done about it?
questions.why: History and prior action. 8D-2025-003, a closed report — the case Phase 2's grouping exists for.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: Why has the sealer skip problem on door hem flanges not been closed yet?
questions.why: An explanation of an open investigation's status. 8D-2026-004 D4 and D7.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: What is being done to stop weld nugget problems recurring at SUP-004?
questions.why: Prevention, D7 of 8D-2026-002. A forward-looking action, not a number.

questions.label: BOTH
questions.question: Why is SUP-003's defect rate getting worse?
questions.why: Rule case 1 — a number that needs its cause. SQL shows the climb from 899 to 1,586 PPM; only 8D-2026-011 says electrode tip wear after a controller replacement. SQL alone gives a trend with no reason; docs alone give a reason with no evidence it is happening.

questions.label: BOTH
questions.question: SUP-001's PPM rose sharply in mid-2026. Should we raise a corrective action request?
questions.why: Rule case 2 — a claim needing corroboration, and the sharpest question in the set. SQL shows a real rise (746, 856, 854). 8D-2026-009 says the incoming fixture had drifted out of calibration, supplier CMM data showed the parts conforming, and the recorded PPM overstates the actual rate. SQL alone leads to chasing a supplier who did nothing wrong.

questions.label: BOTH
questions.question: Which suppliers with open 8D reports also have a worsening PPM trend?
questions.why: Rule case 3 — a comparison across both stores. The open-report list is in documents; the trend is in SQL. Neither half is the answer.

questions.label: BOTH
questions.question: Both SUP-001 and SUP-003 show a PPM increase in 2026. Are they the same kind of problem?
questions.why: The pairing the dataset was built for. Identical shape in SQL, opposite correct responses. Distinguishing them is impossible from the tables alone.
questions.variance: Passed run 1, failed runs 2 and 3. Flips between runs, so not treated as a label error — the distinction from BOTH06, which failed consistently.

questions.label: BOTH
questions.question: PN-1042 had a bad month in November 2025. Was it fixed?
questions.why: SQL shows the spike and shows subsequent months back to normal. 8D-2025-007 says why — a single coil, rejected and returned, with elongation testing added. 'Back to normal' and 'fixed' are different claims; only the document supports the second.
questions.variance: Failed runs 1 and 2, passed run 3. Flagged as the weakest BOTH label in the set before any run — a case can be made for DOCS alone, since D6 states the rate returned to baseline. Kept as BOTH because it flips rather than failing consistently.

questions.label: DOCS
questions.question: Is the weld porosity at SUP-003 the same issue as last year?
questions.why: 8D-2026-011's D2 states the problem is recurring, says how it differs from the earlier event, and names 8D-2025-003 by ID. Retrieved alone, that passage answers the question.
questions.relabelled: 2026-09-07, after three router runs. Originally labelled BOTH on the reasoning that the current trend was needed as evidence. The router chose DOCS in all three runs with the same reason each time — unlike BOTH04 and BOTH05, which flip, so this was not variance. Re-reading the document confirmed it does not merely contain evidence for the answer, it is the answer.
questions.counter_argument: The document asserts PPM climbed without showing it. If corroborating numbers were required, BOTH would hold. Rejected because the question asks whether two problems are the same kind, which is a comparison of descriptions — unlike BOTH02, which asks whether to act on a number, where the number matters.

questions.label: NEITHER
questions.question: What is SUP-003's on-time delivery rate?
questions.why: No delivery data in the schema and no document mentions it. Measured: closest retrieval distance 0.3851, outside the 0.35 threshold.

questions.label: NEITHER
questions.question: Which operator was on shift when the D-WLD-01 defects were found?
questions.why: No operator or shift data. line_station is a location, not a person.

questions.label: NEITHER
questions.question: Why did SUP-011's PPM spike in March 2026?
questions.why: False premise. SUP-011 does not exist — ten suppliers, SUP-001 to SUP-010.
questions.baseline_note: Baseline routed this to DOCS — a quiet miss. After the BOTH criterion was made bidirectional it routed to BOTH and claimed SQL held PPM data confirming a spike for SUP-011, which is a confident assertion about data that does not exist. Kept as a miss rather than reclassified, because the fix was a real change to the router: the supplier list is now in the prompt. Fixed in change 2.

questions.label: NEITHER
questions.question: What is the unit cost of the parts SUP-005 supplies?
questions.why: No cost data anywhere in the schema or the reports.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: How many defects did SUP-003 have?
questions.why: Ambiguous on metric — events or units? — and on window. Per the rule, metric ambiguity is not a routing question: it routes to SQL and the agent states its interpretation. Correct routing here is SQL, not BOTH.

questions.label: SQL
questions.question: Which part is the worst?
questions.why: Ambiguous on metric — worst by PPM or by defect count? Low-runner parts make this sharper, since a part at 800 units can top a PPM ranking meaninglessly. Still SQL: the agent states which metric it used.
